ops.text: audit10 c5 wave 2: the 13 rocks02 touch only 0.4 m under the ground and showed 0.14-0.33 m gaps at it (blender/examples/ring_lip.py). Thirteen rocks03, each over a gap at 3.2 m from the centre, close the lip at the ground; the plugins place rocks03 touching rocks02 (kit-mounts-mined abuts 21), so their crossing is designed. rocks03 seats 0.95-1.05 m deep (bar 1.133) and shows about 0.5 m.

audit10 c5 P4: the spring lip is 13 rocks02 chained round sp-pool at 2.92 m from its centre (sp-ring3 at 2.97 m), each touching the next with no crossing (wb check gaps 0.002-0.031 m); the pool rim is 0.3 m so the lip stands on natural ground. No plugin in the pool places a ring, well or pool-edge set an Argonian village may use (kit-assemblies-mined: whiterun wrpondwall*, imperial mwimparchpool01, volcanic mineralpool* are off-culture or in no published kit)

ops.text: walk 12 wave 2: the lodge's hanging sign (gs-sign) is removed. The lodge is a domed mud pod: every face the beam can meet reads roof-edge (faceNormalZ 0.82-0.95, R127). No post in the pool carries a mined pair for the blackwood board (its twin test against the Whiterun stables board misses by 0.011 m). The standing notice board d9-notice beside the lodge door is the lodge's service board.

walk 9 dressing (dressing.md § 4, Hist village): the village's dead lie under two low cairns north-west of the Hist and north of the spring-keeper's house (burial runs through the Hist: argonia-4e201-state.md:165-167); the east family keeps two hives on their bench and two hens' nests behind the hut; the family hut by the nets dries fish on a rack. Sites from `wb.py site --free --clear 0.7`.

ops.text: 2.9b-p: node.nirnroot. Nirnroot is a very rare plant that grows near water (UESP Lore:Nirnroot; fauna-hazards.md:101 names it in Black Marsh's flora), so one stands on the natural ground just outside the spring's stone lip, 1.2 m from the fill rocks, on the side away from the spring house door.

ops.why: A nirnroot grows by the spring; it is rare and grows only near water. A forager takes it and it grows back slowly.
